([[Tilton, New Hampshire]]) | college = [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] (2012–2016) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2016 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2016]]) * Third-team All-American – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] ([[2015 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2015]]) * [[Karl Malone Award]] (2016) * 2x First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2015, 2016) * Third-team All-Big 12 (2014) * [[Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament|Big 12 Tournament]] MVP ([[2015 Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament|2015]]) * Big 12 All-Rookie team (2013) }} '''Georges Niang''' (born June 17, 1993) is a former American [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. ==High school career== A three-year starter and two-year team captain, Niang capped off his career as one of the greatest players in [[Tilton School|The Tilton School]] history, amassing a school-record 2,372 points. He was a three-time First-Team All-NEPSAC Class AA pick, Niang was the 2012 NEPSAC Class AA Player of the Year.http://nepsac.org/page/3086/article/748 He averaged 25.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game as a senior, averaged 24.2 points and 8.2 rebounds as a junior and led his team to the 2011 NEPSAC Class AA championship with a 72-56 win over St. Mark’s. He was named outstanding player of the tournament, scoring 23 points on 11-of-11 shooting from the field in the championship game. His team lost in the 2011 National Prep Championship to Notre Dame Prep (87-85), as Niang scored 31 points.http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=6201933 He played for the Boston-based BABC AAU team, the same program that featured former [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Cyclone]] and [[NBA]] player [[Will Blalock]]. His BABC squad won the 2011 Nike Peach Jam, one of the best AAU tournaments in the country.http://www.nbadraft.net/2011-nike-peach-jam-top-prospects He was teammates at Tilton and in AAU with Nerlens Noel, they won four NEPSAC titles, one national prep championship, one AAU national championship and one Nike EYBL title in his career. Georges was considered one of the best players on the East Coast, ending his prep career as a consensus national top-100 recruit. He was ranked No. 42 by Lindy’s, No. 56 by [[ESPNU]],http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/102752/georges-niang No. 69 by [[Scout.com]], No. 69 by [[Rivals.com]],http://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Georges-Niang-117208 No. 73 by [[Sporting News]], and No. 81 by [[CBS Sports]] in the 2012 prep national rankings. He also had offers from [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], and [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], eventually committing to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2011}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Georges Niang | position = [[Forward (basketball)|F]] | hometown = [[Methuen, Massachusetts|Methuen, MA]] | highschool = [[Tilton School|The Tilton School]] (NH) | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 210 | 40 = | commitdate = May 5, 2011 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2011 | rivals ref title = TBD 2014 Basketball Commitments | espn ref title = ESPN | rivals school = 19 | espn schoolid = 66 | rivals overall = 6, 16 (F) | espn overall = 56, 2 (NH), 14 (F) | accessdate = 2015-06-14 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Niang was named to the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12 All-Rookie Team]] in his freshman year in 2013. In the second round of the [[2014 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2014 NCAA Tournament]], Niang broke the [[Fifth metatarsal bone|fifth metatarsal]] in his right foot, forcing him to sit for the remainder of the event.{{cite web|title=Georges Niang Bio|url=http://www.cyclones.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205435883|website=Cyclones.com|accessdate=30 July 2014}} As a sophomore, he averaged 16.7 points and 4.5 rebounds as the third most prominent offensive weapon for Iowa State behind [[Melvin Ejim]] and [[DeAndre Kane]].{{cite news|last1=Forgrave|first1=Reid|title=Gorgeous Georges? Iowa State's Niang will look a lot different this season|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/gorgeous-georges-iowa-state-s-niang-will-look-a-lot-different-this-season-101714|accessdate=5 May 2015|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=17 October 2014}} Niang cut back on his calorie consumption in the 2014 offseason and consequently slimmed down to 230 pounds from 260 pounds. As a junior, Niang led the team in scoring with 15.3 points per game to go along with 5.4 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game. Seeded third in the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2015 NCAA Tournament]], the Cyclones were upset by 14th seeded [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|UAB]] in the round of 64 despite 11 points and seven rebounds from Niang. He considered entering the [[2015 NBA Draft]], but instead decided to return for his senior season. "I was weighing it, but I want to be loyal to the program and didn't want to go out this way," Niang said. "I didn't want to leave my mark like that."{{cite news|title=Iowa State's Georges Niang says he's returning next
